text:
Maya: Heads up from yesterday's customer sync — they want per-route eval thresholds plus an automatic rollback flow if a model drops below a critical metric. They're asking for this in the pilot ask.
Devin: Do we have precedent for auto-rollback? I thought eval-alerting was notify-only in our pilot plan. Link: https://go/redwood/internal/optimize/alerts-design
Sarah: Correct, pilot assumed notifications and playbook for manual rollback. Auto-rollback introduces risk (false positives, flapping) and needs SRE/ops runbooks, canary timing, and audit trails.
Liam: Also hearing another customer wants quantization artifacts they can run on-prem to validate perf/quality. Essentially they want an exportable profile + a tiny verification tool.
Maya: Two distinct asks: auto-rollback on major regression, and on-prem quant validation. We need to decide pilot scope.
Devin: My suggested compromise for MVP: 1) Ship per-prompt-set eval alerts with severity tags (info/warn/critical) and clear escalation steps, 2) Document manual rollback steps + provide a one-click manual rollback UI, 3) Provide hosted quant profiles and example artifacts for customers to test, 4) Offer an unsupported "export runner" script they can use on-prem — no validation from Redwood. Defer any certified on-prem quant verification and automated rollback to Dedicated/Private roadmap.
Sarah: +1 to deferring. We must put explicit language in the acceptance criteria and sales-facing docs so SEs don't promise auto-rollback or on-prem validation.
Liam: For the export runner we can produce a minimal tarball: profile.pb, sample inputs, and a readme. Label it "unsupported - use at your own risk". I'll prototype the runner and a README snippet.
Maya: Acceptance checklist proposal for pilot (draft):
- Eval alerts: per-prompt-set scoping, severity mapping (info/warn/critical), email/console notifications.
- Rollback: manual rollback path with UI and a runbook explaining when to trigger it; audit log entry for rollbacks.
- Recommendations: batching & caching guidance + a small sim run and suggested config YAML per workload type.
- Quant: hosted quant profiles + example artifacts; export runner (unsupported).
- Comms: Release notes + sales FAQ calling out which items are deferred.
Devin: Let's also capture metric comparison semantics: whether thresholds are absolute or relative delta, windowing, and smoothing. I can draft a short RFC on diff calculation and severity thresholds.
Sarah: I'll update the pilot PR's acceptance section and the public FAQ. Also will include wording for "unsupported export runner" so Sales knows not to promise validation.
Liam: Example runner usage I'll add to the README:
```bash
# unsupported quant profile runner (example)
./quant_export_runner --profile /tmp/profile.pb --model /mnt/models/foo --test-corpus ./prompts.json
```
Devin: Timeline: can we hit a gating PR in 6 business days if we scope as above? I want to avoid pushing pilot by adding on-prem validation or auto-rollback.
Maya: 6 days sounds tight but doable if teams limit scope. I'll file the gating PR now and tag owners.
ops-bot: release-bot added card #optimize-pilot-4837 to board and assigned to Maya
QA-bot: QA note: require a smoke eval run using a sanitized customer prompt set before marking pilot accepted
Maya: I'll attach a sanitized sample prompt bundle to the PR and assign QA.
Devin: Follow-ups: (A) I'll write the diff/RFC and severity mapping table, (B) Liam to provide export runner artifact and README, (C) Sarah to update comms and sales FAQ, (D) Maya to finalize gating checklist and open PR.
Sarah: Adding a short blurb for Sales: "Pilot provides alerts and manual rollback. Automated rollback and on-prem quant validation are planned for post-pilot Dedicated/Private releases."
Liam: Will push a small prototype artifact and README to the pilot assets folder.
Maya: Thanks — closing thread. If a customer insists on auto-rollback we escalate to product leadership to decide whether to accelerate Dedicated work.
